title: Livonian Conference
capsule: The Livonian Confederation (Livländischer Städtebund) was a loose political alliance of five ecclesiastical and secular territorial lords in the eastern Baltic — the Livonian Order, the Archbishopric of Riga, the Bishopric of Dorpat, the Bishopric of Ösel-Wiek, and the Bishopric of Courland — which co-existed and negotiated collectively from the late 14th century onward, formalised through regular diets (Herrentage) from 1422. It was a fragile structure, perpetually divided by conflicts between the Order and the Archbishop of Riga. The confederation collapsed during the Livonian War (1558–1583): Ivan IV of Russia invaded in 1558, and the member territories submitted to Poland-Lithuania, Sweden, and Denmark by 1561–64.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The territorial extent of the Livonian Confederation and its member entities is relatively well documented through German-language chronicles, papal correspondence, and the records of the Livonian diet, though internal boundaries between member states fluctuated.
